Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{7}{3},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{7}{3}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \frac{7}{3} & =\frac{4x-1}{x+1} \\ 7(x+1) & =3(4x-1) \\ 7x+7 & =12x-3 \\ 7x-12x & =-3-7 \\ -5x & =-10 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =x+1=2+1=3, \\ BC & =4x-1=4(2)-1=7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 7 \\  & =10.5.\end{aligned}
$$
